Start with variant-level association summaries. Check their structure and study context, inspect the figures, verify one result and explain what the evidence supports.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## One workflow for every dataset

1. **Define the question** and identify the study design.
2. **Preview the results** you will produce.
3. **Meet the inputs**, including alleles, effect units and genome build.
4. **Check the inputs** and document exclusions.
5. **Run the analysis** with recorded parameters.
6. **Verify and explain** figures using numerical evidence.
7. **Write the report**, including evidence and limitations.
:::

| Route | Status | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| [Synthetic practice](examples/synthetic/00-start-here.qmd) | Runnable; fictional data and ten figures included | Learn the workflow and independently verify a variant |
| [Real study](examples/real-study/00-start-here.qmd) | Scaffold; dataset not yet selected | Prepare a verified quantitative-trait case study |
| [Your own study](examples/my-study/00-start-here.qmd) | Input contract and commands provided | Apply the same checks to compatible data |

## Scope

This first version analyses **quantitative-trait beta summary statistics for autosomal single-nucleotide variants**. It does not fit an association model to genotypes. Binary-trait odds ratios, sex chromosomes, indels, fine mapping, LD clumping and polygenic scores need additional methods and inputs.

A summary-statistics row is a **variant association**, not a participant. Multiple nearby associations can reflect correlated variants; a peak does not identify a causal variant or gene.

::: {.callout-important}
## Scaffold release

The synthetic example runs now. Real-study pages are preparation checkpoints, not completed lessons with biological findings. Expanded teaching content and additional figures will follow after verified data selection.
:::
